_comment: BRIDGE-1 CAMPAIGN BUILD MANIFEST — SuperDSC -> DataflowIR.
⛔⛔ READ THIS FILE AS YOUR BRIEF. The translator prompt names only this file, the worklist, the
campaign-wide Wavefront config and your worktree — it does NOT name AGENT-BRIEF.md, so anything
written only there never reaches you. This file was BRIDGE 2's until now; measured on the bridge-3
campaign, two agents ran a whole batch against a sibling campaign's instructions for exactly this
reason.
There is no C build, no shim and no FFI boundary: this is a pure-logic port into the EXISTING crate
crates/compiler/deeptools. `configure` is a no-op and the C-side gates in the playbook do not apply.
⛔ TRANSLATOR GATE — EXACTLY these two, from the repo root, ONCE PER BATCH at the end:
cargo check -p deeptools
cargo test  -p deeptools
Never the workspace or acceptance build: a worktree's target/ is ~6 GB and this host has under
60 GB free. The orchestrator owns that gate.
═══ WHAT YOU ARE PORTING ═══
110 units. 106 are dsc-based-utils/DSC2ToDataflowIR — the conversion, whose header guard is
literally SUPERDSCTODATAFLOWIR and whose constructor takes a SuperDsc*. The other 4 are the DDL/DSC
DERIVATIONS that scratchy currently INVENTS in shape.rs, which is the defect this campaign removes:
ddc/ddcv1.cpp:792 checkConstraints (contains checkConstraintsImpl at :825 — one unit),
ddc/ddcv1.cpp:3283 createDataConnectMetadata, and dsc/dsc2.cpp:4109
DesignSpaceConfig::getCumulativeStickSizes over dsc/dsc2.cpp:4066 getStickSizes.
⚠ ddcv1.cpp:789 and :1723 are CALL SITES of getCumulativeStickSizes, not its definition.
INPUT SIDE, already typed: scratchy's own SuperDSC in
crates/targets/spyre/src/lower_subtile_tape_to_superdsc.rs, carrying SdscOp / SdscFolds with
C++-mirroring field names (opConsts, backGapCore_, coordinates_, constantInfo_), validated against
the vendor's dxp_standalone. ⚠ Several fields are untyped serde_json::Value escape hatches; a port
that reads one needs it TYPED, and tightening those is IN SCOPE — say so in the commit message.
OUTPUT SIDE: the existing crates/compiler/deeptools/src/islands/dataflow_ir/.
AUTHORITY: /Users/nickm/git/deeptools-src/<file>:<line> (revision a0d29abbed).
⛔ /Users/nickm/git/deeptools is a DIFFERENT revision — do not use it.
✅ The extract crustify-bridge1/cpp/bridge1.cpp is VERIFIED UNTRUNCATED, 110 of 110, by
tools/verify_extract.py, which shares no code with the extractor and whose two negative controls
both fail as required. Still cite the authority.
═══ HARD CAPS — MEASURED, NOT GUIDANCE ═══
Bridge 2's first 144 functions cost 43 HOURS of wall clock, 89% of it model time, 586 MILLION
cache-read tokens against 5 million output — 30 to 48 turns per function. Of 30,991 lines produced,
only 5,306 were implementation: 12,333 were doc comments and 12,575 were tests. 82% of the output
was not the port. So, per ported function:
doc comment lines        8   — the `/// Replaces: eNNN_name` anchor, one line of what it does,
and any TRAP. Nothing else. NO TUTORIALS.
test functions           1   — or 2 where the vendor's own case plus one negative both apply
cargo check / test       once per BATCH, at the end — NOT per function
⛔ DO NOT RE-VERIFY CITATIONS — take the file:line from crustify-bridge1/UNITS.tsv as given; the
review pass owns that check.
⛔ DO NOT GREP THE CRATE TO DISCOVER TYPES — your .rs home's header names what your units need.
⭐ NOT CAPPED: correctness and the emission. Cutting the port to hit a cap is worse than being slow.
═══ WHAT "PORTED" MEANS ═══
The WHOLE function, INCLUDING ITS EMISSION. A hand attempt on bridge 2 extracted each function's
decision rule into a documented predicate — is_l3(), BurstSetting::of(), Granularity::checked() —
left out the part that emits the op, and reported it done. Nothing called any of it. The op a
function emits IS the function, with its exact attribute names and values, branch order and early
returns. Droppable: the mechanism for REACHING operands (walking uses, memoising by
(core, corelet, component), positioning an OpBuilder). If the island cannot express a function's
input, EXTEND THE ISLAND — deciding a function is unnecessary is not the porter's call.
═══ CRATE RULES (crates/compiler/deeptools/CLAUDE.md) ═══
🛑 NEVER RUNTIME REFUSE: no Result, no Err(, no .ok_or, no assert!, no debug_assert!. A closed set
is an enum; an invariant is a type. `todo!` naming unported work is allowed.
⛔ NEWTYPES, never raw scalars. NO STRINGS for closed sets. Arch / Model / Workload flow through.
No bindgen, no -sys, no ffi_export, no extern "C", no Foo/FooRef/FooMut, no unsafe, no sanitizers —
whatever the generic C-porting conventions in your system prompt say about those.
